description: An introduction to electric current, voltage, resistance, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits, and basic domestic wiring safety.

options.text: The force pushing charge through a wire
The rate of flow of electric charge
The energy stored in a battery

mcq.explanation: Current is the rate of flow of electric charge. Exam Tip: Current (I) = charge (Q) / time (t). SI unit: ampere (A).

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of electric current is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of current is the ampere. Exam Tip: Current is measured with an ammeter, in amperes.

mcq.questionText: The instrument used to measure electric current in a circuit is the:
mcq.explanation: An ammeter measures current. Exam Tip: Ammeter (current, series) vs voltmeter (voltage, parallel).

mcq.questionText: The instrument used to measure potential difference (voltage) is the:
mcq.explanation: A voltmeter measures potential difference. Exam Tip: Voltmeter connected in parallel across the component.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of potential difference (voltage) is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of voltage is the volt. Exam Tip: Volt (V) = voltage; ampere (A) = current; ohm = resistance.

mcq.questionText: The opposition offered by a conductor to the flow of electric current is called:
mcq.explanation: Opposition to current flow is resistance. Exam Tip: Resistance (ohms) slows current, converting electrical energy to heat.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of resistance is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of resistance is the ohm. Exam Tip: Ohm (symbol Omega), named after Georg Ohm.

mcq.questionText: According to Ohm's law, at constant temperature, the current through a conductor is:

options.text: Directly proportional to the voltage across it

mcq.explanation: V = IR, so current increases as voltage increases (constant resistance). Exam Tip: Ohm's law: V = IR. Double the voltage, double the current.

mcq.questionText: Using Ohm's law V = IR, if a current of 2 A flows through a resistor of 5 ohms, the voltage across it is:
mcq.explanation: V = 2 x 5 = 10 V. Exam Tip: Multiply current by resistance.

mcq.questionText: If the voltage across a resistor is 12 V and the current through it is 3 A, the resistance is:
mcq.explanation: R = V/I = 12/3 = 4 ohms. Exam Tip: R = V/I - a common rearrangement of V = IR.

mcq.questionText: In a series circuit, the current at every point in the circuit is:
mcq.explanation: Series circuits have one path, so the same current flows everywhere. Exam Tip: Series: same current, voltage shares between components.

mcq.questionText: In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each branch is:

options.text: The same as the supply voltage

mcq.explanation: Each parallel branch gets the full supply voltage. Exam Tip: Parallel: same voltage across each branch, current splits.

mcq.questionText: A fuse in a domestic electrical circuit is used to:

options.text: Break the circuit automatically when current is too high, preventing fire

mcq.explanation: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit if current exceeds a safe level. Exam Tip: A fuse is a thin wire that melts (blows) under excess current.

mcq.questionText: In domestic electrical wiring, the wire connected to the earth for safety is called the:
mcq.explanation: The safety wire connected to the ground is the earth wire. Exam Tip: Three wires: live (carries current), neutral (completes circuit), earth (safety).

mcq.questionText: The force that drives electric charge around a complete circuit, supplied by a cell or battery, is called the:
mcq.explanation: This driving force is the electromotive force (e.m.f.), measured in volts. Exam Tip: E.m.f. is the energy given to each unit of charge by the source.

fib.questionText: Electric current is the rate of flow of __________.
fib.explanation: Current is defined as the rate of flow of electric charge. Exam Tip: Current = charge / time.

fib.questionText: The SI unit of electric current is the __________.
fib.explanation: The ampere (A) is the SI unit of current, measured using an ammeter. Exam Tip: Symbol A. Measured with an ammeter.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure current, connected in series in a circuit, is the __________.
fib.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series to measure the current flowing through a circuit. Exam Tip: Ammeter -> series connection.

fib.questionText: The instrument used to measure voltage, connected in parallel across a component, is the __________.
fib.explanation: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across a component to measure potential difference. Exam Tip: Voltmeter -> parallel connection.

fib.questionText: The opposition to the flow of current in a conductor is called __________.
fib.explanation: Resistance is the opposition a conductor offers to current flow, measured in ohms. Exam Tip: Measured in ohms.

fib.questionText: Ohm's law is written as the equation V = __________.
fib.explanation: Ohm's law states voltage equals current multiplied by resistance, V = IR. Exam Tip: V = IR (voltage = current x resistance).

fib.questionText: In a series circuit, the current is the __________ (same/different) at every point.
fib.explanation: A series circuit has a single path, so the same current flows through every point. Exam Tip: Series: one path, same current throughout.

fib.questionText: In a parallel circuit, the voltage across each branch is the __________ as the supply voltage.
fib.explanation: Each branch in a parallel circuit is connected directly across the supply, so it receives the full supply voltage. Exam Tip: Parallel: same voltage, current splits.

fib.questionText: A safety device that melts and breaks a circuit when the current is too high is called a __________.
fib.explanation: A fuse contains a thin wire that melts when the current exceeds a safe limit, breaking the circuit. Exam Tip: The fuse blows to protect the circuit and prevent fires.

fib.questionText: In domestic wiring, the wire that provides a safety path to the ground is called the __________ wire.
fib.explanation: The earth wire connects the appliance casing to the ground, providing a safe path for fault current. Exam Tip: Earth wire protects against electric shock if a fault occurs.

tf.questionText: Electric current is the rate of flow of electric charge.
tf.explanation: This is the definition of electric current. Exam Tip: Measured in amperes with an ammeter.

tf.questionText: The ammeter is connected in parallel to measure current.
tf.explanation: An ammeter must be connected in series, not parallel, to measure current. Exam Tip: The ammeter is connected in series.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of resistance is the ohm.
tf.explanation: Resistance is measured in ohms. Exam Tip: Named after Georg Simon Ohm.

tf.questionText: According to Ohm's law, current is inversely proportional to voltage.
tf.explanation: Ohm's law states current is directly proportional to voltage at constant resistance, not inversely. Exam Tip: Current is directly proportional to voltage (constant R).

tf.questionText: In a series circuit, the current is the same at every point.
tf.explanation: Because there is only one path for current in a series circuit, the current is identical throughout. Exam Tip: Voltage, not current, is shared in a series circuit.

tf.questionText: In a parallel circuit, all branches carry the same current.
tf.explanation: In a parallel circuit the current splits between branches; only the voltage is the same across each branch. Exam Tip: Current splits between branches; voltage stays the same.

tf.questionText: A fuse protects a circuit by breaking it when the current becomes too high.
tf.explanation: The fuse wire melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds its rating. Exam Tip: This prevents overheating and electrical fires.

tf.questionText: The earth wire in domestic wiring carries the main current to power an appliance.
tf.explanation: The live wire carries the operating current; the earth wire is only a safety path. Exam Tip: The live wire carries the current; earth is a safety wire.

tf.questionText: Electromotive force (e.m.f.) is supplied by a cell or battery to drive current around a circuit.
tf.explanation: The e.m.f. is the energy supplied by the source to drive charge around the circuit. Exam Tip: E.m.f. is measured in volts, like potential difference.

tf.questionText: The voltmeter is connected in series with the component being measured.
tf.explanation: A voltmeter must be connected in parallel across a component, not in series. Exam Tip: The voltmeter is connected in parallel.

summary.correctAnswer: The rate of flow of electric charge through a conductor, measured in amperes (A).
summary.explanation: Current is caused by the movement of charged particles, usually electrons, through a wire. Exam Tip: I = Q/t; use an ammeter in series to measure it.

summary.correctAnswer: An instrument used to measure electric current, connected in series in a circuit.
summary.explanation: Ammeters have very low resistance so they do not reduce the current they measure. Exam Tip: Always connect an ammeter in series, never in parallel.

summary.correctAnswer: An instrument used to measure potential difference (voltage), connected in parallel across a component.
summary.explanation: Voltmeters have very high resistance so they draw negligible current from the circuit. Exam Tip: Always connect a voltmeter in parallel across the component.

summary.correctAnswer: The opposition offered by a conductor to the flow of electric current, measured in ohms.
summary.explanation: Resistance converts some electrical energy into heat as current flows. Exam Tip: R = V/I.

summary.correctAnswer: The current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it at constant temperature, written V = IR.
summary.explanation: Ohm's law links voltage, current and resistance, and holds only if temperature stays constant. Exam Tip: Rearrange as I = V/R or R = V/I when needed.

summary.correctAnswer: A circuit in which components are connected end to end along a single path, so the same current flows through each one.
summary.explanation: In a series circuit, the supply voltage is shared among the components. Exam Tip: If one component fails, the whole circuit breaks.

summary.correctAnswer: A circuit in which components are connected across separate branches, so each branch has the full supply voltage.
summary.explanation: In a parallel circuit, the total current splits between the branches according to each branch's resistance. Exam Tip: Household wiring uses parallel circuits so appliances work independently.

summary.correctAnswer: A safety device containing a thin wire that melts and breaks the circuit when the current exceeds a safe value.
summary.explanation: Fuses are rated in amperes and chosen to match the normal operating current of an appliance. Exam Tip: A blown fuse must be replaced, not repaired, before use.

summary.correctAnswer: A safety wire in domestic wiring that connects the metal casing of an appliance to the ground.
summary.explanation: If a fault causes the casing to become live, the earth wire provides a low-resistance path that trips the fuse or circuit breaker. Exam Tip: The earth wire is colored green and yellow and carries no current in normal operation.

summary.correctAnswer: The energy given to each unit of charge by a cell or battery to drive it around a complete circuit, measured in volts.
summary.explanation: E.m.f. is the total energy supplied per unit charge, including energy lost to the internal resistance of the source. Exam Tip: E.m.f. is always slightly greater than the terminal voltage due to internal resistance.

hoq.questionText: A resistor is connected to a 12 V battery, and an ammeter in series reads 4 A. Calculate the resistance, and state what happens to the current if resistance doubles (voltage unchanged).

options.text: R = 3 ohms; doubling R halves the current to 2 A
R = 48 ohms; doubling R doubles the current
R = 3 ohms; doubling R doubles the current
R = 16 ohms; current stays the same

hoq.explanation: R = V/I = 12/4 = 3 ohms. If R doubles to 6 ohms, new current = 12/6 = 2 A - half the original. Exam Tip: Current is inversely proportional to resistance (constant voltage) - double R, halve I.

hoq.questionText: Circuit A has two identical bulbs in SERIES; Circuit B has the same bulbs in PARALLEL, both to identical batteries. Compare brightness.

options.text: Bulbs in A are brighter because current is higher there
Bulbs in B are brighter because each bulb gets the full battery voltage, while in A the voltage is shared between the two bulbs, giving each less voltage and a dimmer glow
Bulbs in A do not light at all

hoq.explanation: In series, voltage is shared between bulbs (dimmer). In parallel, each bulb gets the full supply voltage (brighter). Exam Tip: This is why household circuits use parallel wiring.

hoq.questionText: A household circuit is protected by a 13 A fuse. An iron (2000 W), kettle (2500 W), and lamp (100 W) are plugged into the same socket at 230 V mains. Using I = P/V, determine if the fuse will blow.

options.text: Total current is about 20 A, which exceeds 13 A, so the fuse will blow, protecting the circuit from overheating
Total current is only 2 A, well within the fuse rating
The fuse rating does not matter
Total power determines the fuse rating directly in watts

hoq.explanation: Iron: 2000/230=8.7A; kettle: 2500/230=10.9A; lamp: 100/230=0.4A. Total = 8.7+10.9+0.4 = 20 A, exceeding 13 A. Exam Tip: Convert each appliance's power to current with I=P/V, then add currents sharing a socket. Exceeding the rating blows the fuse - a safety success.
